# gvisor plugin fields

<!-- Generated by tools/genfields from pkg/gvisor/fields.go. Do not edit; run make generate. -->

Fields reuse Falco's standard names wherever the meaning matches, so existing
rule knowledge transfers. A field is absent (`<NA>` in outputs) when the
event does not carry it, for example `fd.name` on `sentry_execve`.

Differences from Falco's syscall source:

- `proc.pid`/`proc.ppid` are ids inside the sandbox, not host pids.
- `proc.tty` is approximated from the stdio fds at exec.
- `fd.name` for `connect` is the remote endpoint (`ip:port`); the local
  side is not reported by gVisor.
- `evt.arg.*` values are rendered strings (`O_WRONLY|O_CREAT`, `AF_PACKET`).
- `evt.res` is `SUCCESS` or the errno name, as in Falco. There is no `evt.rawres`:
  plugin fields have no signed integer type to carry negative return values.
- `proc.aname`/`proc.aexepath` require an index; use `gvisor.anames` to
  match any ancestor.
- Container metadata (name, image, labels, k8s) is resolved asynchronously.
  A new container's first event waits up to `metadataWaitMillis` for it.
- String fields carry the workload's bytes unchanged, so rules match what the
  workload actually ran. Falco escapes control characters when rendering
  outputs (verified with Falco 0.45: a newline in argv appears as `\n`),
  so they cannot forge alert lines.

## Event

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `evt.type` | string | Syscall name (e.g. connect, execve) or sentry point: container_start, sentry_clone, sentry_execve, task_exit, exit_notify_parent, gvisor_stats. |
| `evt.res` | string | SUCCESS, or the errno name (e.g. ENOENT) when the syscall failed. Only on syscall exit points. |
| `evt.failed` | bool | True when the syscall returned an error. |
| `evt.is_open_read` | bool | True for open events whose access mode allows reading. |
| `evt.is_open_write` | bool | True for open events whose access mode allows writing. |
| `evt.arg.flags` | string | Open flags rendered like Falco, e.g. O_WRONLY\|O_CREAT\|O_TRUNC. |
| `evt.arg.domain` | string | Socket domain, e.g. AF_INET, AF_PACKET. |
| `evt.arg.type` | string | Socket type, e.g. SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_RAW. |
| `evt.arg.request` | string | ptrace request, e.g. PTRACE_ATTACH. |
| `evt.arg.uid` | uint64 | setuid: requested uid. |
| `evt.arg.gid` | uint64 | setgid: requested gid. |
| `evt.arg.ruid` | uint64 | setresuid: requested real uid (4294967295 means unchanged). |
| `evt.arg.euid` | uint64 | setresuid: requested effective uid (4294967295 means unchanged). |
| `evt.arg.suid` | uint64 | setresuid: requested saved uid (4294967295 means unchanged). |
| `evt.arg.rgid` | uint64 | setresgid: requested real gid (4294967295 means unchanged). |
| `evt.arg.egid` | uint64 | setresgid: requested effective gid (4294967295 means unchanged). |
| `evt.arg.sgid` | uint64 | setresgid: requested saved gid (4294967295 means unchanged). |

## File descriptor

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fd.name` | string | File path for open/execve, ip:port of the remote endpoint for connect/accept, local endpoint for bind/listen, or unix socket path. |
| `fd.nameraw` | string | Path exactly as passed to the syscall, before fd_path resolution. |
| `fd.directory` | string | Directory part of fd.name for file events. |
| `fd.filename` | string | Base name of fd.name for file events. |
| `fd.type` | string | file, ipv4, ipv6, unix or netlink. |
| `fd.typechar` | string | One-character fd type: f, 4, 6, u, n. |
| `fd.sip` | ipaddr | Server IP: the connect target, or the bound address for bind/listen. |
| `fd.sport` | uint64 | Server port. |
| `fd.rip` | ipaddr | Remote IP: the connect target or the accepted peer. |
| `fd.rport` | uint64 | Remote port. |
| `fd.l4proto` | string | tcp, udp or raw for IPv4 and IPv6 sockets whose type is known: on socket and listen, and on connect when the socket() call that created the fd was seen. Absent for other families (Unix, netlink, packet) and when the type is unknown. |

## Process and user

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `proc.pid` | uint64 | Thread-group id inside the sandbox. |
| `proc.ppid` | uint64 | Parent thread-group id inside the sandbox. |
| `proc.name` | string | Process name (comm, up to 15 characters). |
| `proc.exe` | string | First command-line argument (argv[0]). |
| `proc.exepath` | string | Full path of the executable. |
| `proc.args` | string | Command-line arguments after argv[0], space separated. |
| `proc.cmdline` | string | proc.name followed by proc.args. |
| `proc.cwd` | string | Current working directory. |
| `proc.tty` | uint64 | Approximate controlling terminal: pts device number when stdio is a /dev/pts/N, 1 for other terminals, 0 for none. |
| `proc.pname` | string | Parent process name. |
| `proc.pexepath` | string | Parent executable path. |
| `proc.pcmdline` | string | Parent command line. |
| `proc.aname[N]` | string | Name of the Nth ancestor: [0] is the process, [1] its parent, up to [8]. |
| `proc.aexepath[N]` | string | Executable path of the Nth ancestor. |
| `proc.is_exe_upper_layer` | bool | True when the executable was written to the container's upper (writable) layer. |
| `proc.is_exe_lower_layer` | bool | True when the executable exists on the container image (overlay lower) layer. False for files created at runtime, including on tmpfs mounts such as /dev/shm and the /tmp tmpfs runsc mounts over an empty image /tmp. |
| `proc.is_exe_from_memfd` | bool | True when the executable is a memfd (fileless execution). |
| `proc.stdin.type` | string | fd type of stdin at exec: file, directory, pipe, unix, ipv4, ipv6. |
| `proc.stdout.type` | string | fd type of stdout at exec. |
| `proc.stderr.type` | string | fd type of stderr at exec. |
| `proc.sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the executable, hex encoded (requires binary_sha256 on sentry/execve). |
| `user.uid` | uint64 | Effective user id. |
| `group.gid` | uint64 | Effective group id. |

## Container and Kubernetes

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `container.id` | string | Container id truncated to 12 characters. |
| `container.full_id` | string | Full container id. |
| `container.name` | string | Container name from the runtime; empty until metadata is resolved. |
| `container.image` | string | Container image from the runtime; empty until metadata is resolved. |
| `container.label[key]` | string | Container label value, filtered by labelAllowlist. |
| `k8s.pod.name` | string | Kubernetes pod name (cri provider). |
| `k8s.ns.name` | string | Kubernetes namespace (cri provider). |
| `k8s.pod.label[key]` | string | Kubernetes pod label value (cri provider), filtered by labelAllowlist. |

## gVisor

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gvisor.container_id` | string | Container id reported by gVisor. |
| `gvisor.is_exec_session` | bool | True when the process descends from a 'runsc exec' (docker/kubectl exec) session. |
| `gvisor.sysno` | uint64 | Raw syscall number for syscall points. |
| `gvisor.point` | string | gVisor trace point, e.g. syscall/connect/exit or sentry/execve. |
| `gvisor.anames` | list of string | Names of all known ancestors, nearest first; use with intersects / in. |
| `gvisor.exit_status` | uint64 | task_exit and exit_notify_parent points: the thread group's Linux wait status as gVisor reports it, not the exit code. The exit code is exit_status >> 8 (exit_group(1) gives 256); a death by signal has the signal number in the low 7 bits. A task_exit of a thread while its group still runs carries the group's status, usually 0. |
| `gvisor.prev_uid` | uint64 | setuid-family events: the effective uid the process had before the call. Absent if the process had not been seen before. |
| `gvisor.is_exec_fallback` | bool | True on the first event of a process after an execve/execveat whose sentry/execve point was not received (dropped by gVisor) but which did happen: gVisor reports the syscall exit before loading the image, so the exec only counts once a later event shows the task renamed to the new program. Exec rules can match it in place of sentry_execve. proc.* describes the new program; binary details (layer flags, hash, stdio) are absent. An exec of a program with the same name as the old one cannot be confirmed this way. |
| `gvisor.stdin_pipe_proc` | string | Name of the process writing to this process's stdin pipe at exec, e.g. curl in curl \| sh. Set only if the writer is still running when the reader execs (gVisor inspects live siblings), and requires pipe_proc_info on sentry/execve. |

## Stats (`evt.type = gvisor_stats`)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gvisor.stats.connections` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: live sandbox connections. |
| `gvisor.stats.events_per_second` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: events per second since the previous stats event. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: total dropped points. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_interval` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points dropped since the previous gvisor_stats event. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_channel_full` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points dropped because the event queue's total budget (maxQueueBytes) was full. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_queue_share` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points dropped because one sandbox used its fair share of the event queue (maxQueueBytes divided by connected sandboxes). |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_truncated` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points dropped for exceeding maxEventSize. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_decode_error` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points dropped as undecodable. |
| `gvisor.stats.drops_sandbox` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: points the sandbox reported dropping on its side. |
| `gvisor.stats.attach_attempts` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: attach attempts. |
| `gvisor.stats.attach_failures` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: failed attach attempts. |
| `gvisor.stats.queue_bytes` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: bytes of events waiting for Falco (bounded by maxQueueBytes). |
| `gvisor.stats.unmonitored_sandboxes` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: running sandboxes the last attacher sweep found unconnected and failed to attach. |
| `gvisor.stats.panics` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: panics recovered inside the plugin (each is a bug; the affected point or fetch is dropped). |
| `gvisor.stats.connections_rejected` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: connections refused because maxConnections were open. |
| `gvisor.stats.connections_rejected_interval` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: connections refused since the previous gvisor_stats event. |
| `gvisor.stats.peer_rejected` | uint64 | gvisor_stats: connections refused because the peer was neither root nor Falco's user. |
| `gvisor.stats.attacher_failed` | bool | gvisor_stats: true when the last attacher sweep could not list sandboxes (runsc or its state root unreachable). |
